standard: PCAF (2025). Global GHG Accounting and Reporting Standard Part A: Financed Emissions. Third Edition.
detail: Annex Table 10.1-6 (p.196) — data needs and equations per option
note: Motor vehicle loans are the one Part A class where two options score 1: actual fuel consumption (1a) and make/model efficiency with actual distance travelled (1b) both reach the top of the scale, and Table 10.1-6 confirms it. Its numbers are its own and must never be substituted from another class. The option is decided by what is known about the vehicle and its use: 1a actual fuel or electricity consumed; 1b make/model efficiency × actual distance (an odometer read twice a year apart); 2a make/model efficiency × local statistical distance — and under fn 146 'local' is the province, state or small-country level, so a Sri-Lanka-wide annual-km statistic is local; 2b make/model efficiency × regional statistical distance (a South Asian figure); 3a vehicle-type efficiency × statistical distance; 3b an average vehicle where not even the type is known. Where a borrower's vehicles are assessed under different options, the borrower's score is the lowest data quality in the mix (p.93) — the one class where the standard states a combination rule. The attribution factor is outstanding over the total value at origination (p.91); where that value is unknown the standard's own default is to assume 100 % attribution. Scope 1 is the fuel burned, scope 2 the electricity an electric or plug-in vehicle draws; scope 3 (production, delivery, end of life) is not required, and an institution choosing to report a new vehicle's production emissions reports them as a lump sum under scope 3 in the first year only (p.91). A non-plug-in hybrid consumes petrol only; a plug-in hybrid splits by the manufacturer's usage figure, else a geography split, else 100 % combustion (p.96).
scale: 1 is the highest data quality, 5 the lowest. A score is a category, never a mark out of five.

options.when: Actual fuel consumption (and electricity for electric or plug-in vehicles) over the reporting year is available from the borrower.
The vehicle's make and model efficiency and its actual distance travelled over the year (an odometer read at two dates) are available.

options.family: Option 2: Estimated vehicle emissions from make/model efficiency
options.when: The vehicle's make and model efficiency is available and distance is a local statistic — province, state or small-country level (fn 146).

options.family: Option 2: Estimated vehicle emissions from make/model efficiency
options.when: The vehicle's make and model efficiency is available and distance is a regional statistic.

options.family: Option 3: Estimated vehicle emissions from vehicle type
options.when: Only the vehicle type is known; a vehicle-type average efficiency and a statistical distance are used.

options.family: Option 3: Estimated vehicle emissions from vehicle type
options.when: Not even the vehicle type is known; an average vehicle's efficiency and distance are used.
